facts.statement: The genus Stagonolepis was described by Louis Agassiz in 1844.
The type species of the genus is S. robertsoni, and S. olenkae was described in 2010.
facts.quote: subdivision: S. robertsoni Agassiz 1844 (type) S. olenkae Sulej 2010

facts.statement: Stagonolepis fossils are found in the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic in Germany, Poland, and Scotland.
facts.quote: known from the Late Triassic (Carnian stage) Hassberge Formation of Germany, the Drawno Beds of Poland, and the Lossiemouth Sandstone of Scotland

facts.statement: Stagonolepis robertsoni was approximately 3 meters long.
facts.quote: Stagonolepis robertsoni was about 3 m long

facts.statement: This animal was a quadruped covered in thick armored scales running along its body.
facts.quote: It was a quadrupedal animal covered in thick armoured scales that ran down the length of its body

facts.statement: As a slow-moving browser, it likely used its heavy armor to defend against attacks from carnivorous archosauriforms.
facts.quote: A slow-moving browser, it would have used this heavy body armour to repel attacks from contemporary archosauriform carnivores

facts.statement: The front of its jaws lacked teeth and instead featured an upward-arching beak-like tip.
facts.quote: It had no teeth in the front of its jaws, but instead had a beak-like tip that arched upwards

facts.statement: Its beak-like tip likely allowed it to uproot plants in a manner similar to a modern pig.
facts.quote: This would have allowed it to uproot plants in a similar manner to a modern pig

facts.statement: Peg-like teeth at the back of its mouth were suitable for chewing tough vegetation like horsetails, ferns, and cycads.
facts.quote: The peg-like teeth at the back of its mouth would have been suitable for chewing tough vegetation, including horsetails, ferns, and the newly evolved cycads

facts.statement: A 2018 paper suggested that the forelimb morphology of S. olenkae is an adaptation for scratch-digging.
facts.quote: A 2018 paper suggested that Stagonolepis olenkae's forelimb morphology is an adaptation for scratch-digging

facts.statement: Some researchers question whether S. olenkae is a distinct species, suggesting it may be an example of intraspecific variety like sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: although it is questioned by some researchers and described as an example of intraspecific variety (e. g. sexual dimorphism)

facts.statement: Some paleontologists have considered the South American genus Aetosauroides to be a junior synonym of Stagonolepis.
facts.quote: The genus Aetosauroides from South America has been considered a junior synonym of Stagonolepis by some paleontologists

facts.statement: Most sequential studies conclude that Aetosauroides and Calyptosuchus are valid, monotypic genera distinct from Stagonolepis.
facts.quote: most of the sequential studies conclude that both Aetosauroides and Calyptosuchus are valid and monotypic genera

facts.statement: Stagonolepis is restricted to the Carnian stage of Scotland and Poland.
facts.quote: Stagonolepis is restricted to the Carnian stage of Scotland and Poland

facts.statement: Stagonolepis belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
Stagonolepis is classified within the order Aetosauria.
The time range for Stagonolepis is from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)
